extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A freely available language modeling benchmark constructed from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles. It is available as WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 and retains punctuation, original casing, numbers, and article-level context for learning long-term dependencies. WikiText-103 contains over 103 million tokens; WikiText-2 contains approximately two million training tokens.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.citeAs: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, and Richard Socher. Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843v1 [cs.CL], 26 September 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors selected Wikipedia articles meeting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by Wikipedia editors, resulting in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. These articles had been reviewed by humans and were considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. Text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text extracted from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles using the Wikipedia API. The source Wikipedia markup included macros for metric conversion, abbreviations, language notation, and date handling.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sections primarily featuring lists were removed by default. Sort keys and Edit buttons leaking from HTML were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Words outside the constructed vocabulary were mapped to <unk>.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Normalization and tokenization used the Moses tokenizer, augmented to further split numbers, such as converting 8,600 to 8 @,@ 600, and incorporating additional minor fixes. Vocabulary construction discarded words with counts below three, and out-of-vocabulary words were mapped to <unk>. The dataset was provided in the same format and following the same conventions as the processed Penn Treebank dataset for compatibility with existing language modeling tools, while retaining punctuation, original casing, and numbers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Extracting raw text from Wikipedia markup was described as nontrivial because of extensive macro use. List-heavy sections were removed, mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with placeholder tokens, and words below the vocabulary frequency threshold were mapped to <unk>. The reported out-of-vocabulary token replacement rates are 2.6% for WikiText-2 and 0.4% for WikiText-103.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of language models, particularly evaluation of rare-word prediction and the learning and use of long-term dependencies. WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 share the same validation and test articles, with different vocabularies. WikiText-2 contains 600 training articles, 60 validation articles, and 60 test articles; WikiText-103 contains 28,475 training articles, 60 validation articles, and 60 test articles. The paper evaluates word-level language modeling on WikiText-2 using validation and test perplexity.
